punchline: To win the Olympics, a bid committee paid tuition for relatives of the people who voted.
thirty_sec: Salt Lake City lost the 1998 Winter Games to Nagano and wanted the next ones. Its bid committee paid about $400,000 in scholarships to 13 people from 1991, at least six of them relatives of IOC members, according to a published account. A TV report in November 1998 broke it open. Ten IOC members lost their seats, and the IOC ended member visits to bidding cities.
